g1_mech#1.killer: Whether answers from the patched prompt match answers from the inline-edited prompt, including multi-hop questions that touch superseded text. It must hold before the client rebuilds at 5% patches
g1_mech#1.why: It is cheap and runs client-only, but cache writes and reads still dominate, and the gain is capped at about 1.2× even when every session has an edit.

g1_rf1#1.killer: Share of tokens that must be recomputed under query-driven selection to keep about full accuracy
g1_rf1#1.why: The query-driven approach is prior art (ProphetKV, QCFuse), and the best of it still needs about 7× more recompute than the idea assumes.

g1_neg#2.killer: Cut in turns per task without losing task success
g1_neg#2.why: It attacks the right term, but halving the reads is worth only 1.37×, and the measured turn reduction is short of 2×.

g1_mech#2.killer: Share of post-edit tokens that need full recompute to keep quality
g1_mech#2.why: Against the selective-recompute practice already in LMCache, the gain is about 1.05×. What it adds is mainly the audited quality bound, not lower cost.

g1_ledger#1.killer: mid-document edits per 10-question session needed for the claimed ≥1.5× saving in archetype C
g1_ledger#1.why: The arithmetic holds, but the saving only appears in sessions with about 3 or more mid-document edits, and the quality cost of reading stale text plus a patch (instead of clean text) has not been measured on a real model.

g1_rf2#3.killer: average context after stubbing (the read reduction)
g1_rf2#3.why: The rewrite writes cancel the read savings, and the mechanism itself already exists as Anthropic context editing and JetBrains-style observation masking.

g1_neg#1.killer: answer accuracy when the model reads the original text plus N accumulated patches, compared with clean rewritten text, up to the compaction threshold ε
g1_neg#1.why: It is nearly the same idea as Idea 1 but without a cost-based compaction rule. The saving needs frequent edits, and frequent edits are exactly where PI-LLM-type interference grows.

g1_rf2#1.killer: recompute fraction that keeps quality equal to full recompute
g1_rf2#1.why: Most of the gain is CacheBlend's, which already exists. The ≤10% recompute target is not shown, and a first-token-KL gate may not catch multi-hop accuracy loss, which is the failure ContextPilot reports.
